characters.name: As a whole
characters.description: Conservative Dad, Liberal Mom: In "The New Neighbors", Mama Bear is open to the panda bear neighbors, while Papa Bearis scornful of them because he thinks they're too "different"and because he thinks theirbamboois a "spite fence". Generation Xerox: Papa had the same issues with growing up as Brother and Sister currently do, whether he has admitted to it himself or had others do so on his behalf. He slept with the same night light he later introduced to Sister, and his parents had to resolve issues with him throwing tantrums. Good Parents: Despite his flaws (he has a tendency to boast and can be a greedy eater), Papa Bear is a loving, wise and respected father nonetheless. Papa's good dad traits are especially emphasized in the 2002 series. Mama Bear is a kind and loving mother to her cubs. His Name Really Is "Barkeep": Mama, Papa, Sister and Brother aren't just labels; it's literally their names. Makes it even more bizarre when most of the other characters have normal names. Prior to Sister's birth, Brother was named "Small Bear". Who Names Their Kid "Dude"?: Papa and Mama naming their kids "Sister" and "Brother". By extension, "Papa" and "Mama" count since they were also named accordingly by their parents. At one point during the 2002 show's episode, "The In Crowd", Queenie even lampshades it when she mocks Sister's name.

characters.name: Papa Bear
characters.description: The well-meaning but comically inept patriarch of the Bear Family.First appearance:The Big Honey Hunt Achievements in Ignorance: He's earned several Cub Scout merit badges from Scout Leader Jane by virtue of mishaps that show the Cub Scouts whatnotto do. Aesop Amnesia: Even despite later books depicting him as wiser and more grounded than he was in the early books, the lesson that he shouldn't claim to be an expert on subjects he's not knowledgeable about never sinks in for him no matter how many times he causes trouble for himself. Beware the Nice Ones: Though the much lighter disciplinarian of him and Mama, the cubs know better than to get on his bad side when he'sreallypushed well past his limitations. Big Eater: He is very fond of eating.

characters.name: Mama Bear
characters.description: The level-headed matriarch of the Bear family.First appearance:The Big Honey Hunt Antics-Enabling Wife: Mama tells Papa to do a task like getting honey from the store or buying a Christmas tree, but he would do it the old-fashioned way. She has no other option but to let him drag the cubs on his quest to find something. When Papa didn't get something as planned, he would follow Mama's advice as he should have done in the first place. Deadpan Snarker: Papa has a way of provoking snide remarks from her, like when he asks her how to tell the weather, she responds, "Try this: it's called looking out the window". Disproportionate Retribution: She tried throwing away Brother and Sister's stuff deriding it all as worthless junk when they couldn't agree on how to clean their room. Hair-Trigger Temper: She easily loses her temper, as many book covers show her with an angry expression.

characters.name: Small Bear / Brother Bear
characters.description: The laid-back firstborn cub in the family. Originally named Small Bear in the earliest books, his name changed following Sister's birth.First appearance:The Big Honey Hunt Acquired Situational Narcissism: Has a case of this "Get Stage Fright", boasting about his minor role in the school play. When the big day arrives, he forgets his lines. Sister, who had gotten over stage fright of her own, nudges him in the right direction and saves the play. Age Lift: He is ten years old in the PBS series, rather than eight as in the books. Animal Lover: While it doesn't show up as often as with Sister, he does join in with her on wanting to adopt Little Lady the dog and Gracie the cat in two separate books. Big Brother Bully: Downplayed. Brother usually gets along with and looks out for Sister. He has had a fewJerkass Ballmoments where he teases Sister, most often by scaring her. To be fair, he does get remorseful when realizes when he's gone too far.

characters.name: Sister Bear
characters.description: The hot-blooded second child of the Bear Family.First appearance:New Baby Acquired Situational Narcissism: Sister once got a swelled head when her classmates declared her the best jump-roper in Bear county ("The Jump Rope Contest"). It lasted a day before her friend Lizzie deflated it. Age Lift: She is eight years old in the PBS series, rather than six in the books. All Girls Like Ponies: She wishes for her own horse in the episode "The Wishing Star". Animal Lover: She wants to save the Thanksgiving turkey in one book, was the only one to be sad when Goldie the goldfish died, and was the one totry adopting a baby chipmunk.

characters.name: Honey Bear
characters.description: Adapted Out: She is not featured in the PBS series. Baby Talk: Displays this with such traits as pronouncing "Amen" as "Men" and referring to parakeets as "keets". Beyond that, her mainBaby Talktrait is that she displays short simple sentences and ideas. Cousin Oliver: A recent addition who doesn't usually serve a purpose other than being cute. The Cutie: Quite an adorable cub. Edible Theme Naming: She's named after a sweet substance bees make.

characters.name: Lady
characters.description: Ascended Extra: She's a much more recurring character in the PBS series. Jealous Pet: She was jealous of Gracie when the Bears first adopted her.

characters.name: Grizzly Gramps and Grizzly Gran
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: Gramps is a good-natured elder. Cool Old Lady: Gran is a sweet grandmother. I Was Quite a Looker: The Big Chapter BookAnd The Giddy Grandmagives us a look into Gramps' and Gran's past, where Gran was a vaudeville act called "Wanda the One-Bear Band". Only Known by Their Nickname: Effectively everyone just calls them "Gramps" and "Gran", even their own son Papa, though inThe Berenstain Bear Scouts Save That Backscratcher, Mayor Honeypot reveals Gramps' real name when he recognizes the other bear as "our old friend Ernest". Brother even comments to Gramps afterward that he never knew Gramps' name was Ernest. Only Sane Man: Gramps showed this in theScoutsbooks. He would often be the only adult bear to see through Ralph's scams.

characters.name: Freddy
characters.description: Heterosexual Life-Partners: With Brother; they are best friends. Mister Exposition: Or rather, Mister Definition. Whenever a word comes up that the other cubs don't recognize, they turn to Freddy, who reads the dictionary for fun, for the definition. Nerd Glasses: Highly intelligent and wears glasses.

characters.name: Lizzy Bruin
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: The 2002 series characterizes her as a soft-spokenNice Girl, with her first-meeting with Sister as shown in "Go to School" going off without a hitch unlike in her debut book. Bully Turned Buddy: In her debut book, she and Sister got into a fight because of Lizzy's bossiness, but soon made up and became friends. Heterosexual Life-Partners: With Sister Bear, naturally; the two are best friends. Inconsistent Spelling: In a few books, her name is spelled as Lizzie. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Lizzy can be a little bossy at first when she meets Sister Bear and has trouble getting along with her, but she soon learns how to be nicer to her.

characters.name: Barry Bruin
characters.description: Alliterative Name:BarryBruin. Dumb Jock: He's very athletic, but not very bright. Hidden Depths: As seen in the Big Chapter BookAnd the Ghost of the Auto Graveyard, he has an encyclopedic knowledge of classic car models. Literal-Minded: He often takes analogies literally, such as when he's asked to choose a pen name in the Big Chapter BookAnd the School Scandal Sheet, he picks "Ballpoint. Or maybe fountain."

characters.name: QueenieMcBear
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: HerAlpha Bitchtendencies in the PBS series are almost non-existent, to the pointher role was replaced by another cubin the show's version of "The In-Crowd". Alpha Bitch: Heavily downplayed — she's popular and sometimes shows signs of being a bit snobby, but she mellows out as the series goes on. Awesome, but Impractical: In '"The In-Crowd", her necklaces and earrings do earn her a lot of admiration from the other students. However, later in the story she participates in a jump rope contest and her jewelry gets tangled in the ropes. The narration even lampshades this. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Queenie is this to Ferdy Factual in "The Nerdy Nephew". She at first acts friendly towards him and pretends to be interested in his scientific interests. However, when Too-Tall and his gang attack Ferdy with dodgeballs, Queen laughs deliously at the scene. It was at this moment Ferdy felt a strong sense of betrayal and runs off crying. Bully Turned Buddy: InThe In-Crowd, Queenie is abrasive and dismissive towards Sister when they first meet. After Queenie learns a lesson in humility, she becomes one of Sister's friends.

characters.name: Stacy and Millie
characters.description: Genki Girl: Millie is very peppy. No Full Name Given: Their full names were never revealed. Those Two Girls: Usually seen together and are minor characters.

characters.name: Too-Tall Grizzly
characters.description: The local bully at Bear Country Elementary. He sometimes cons Brother into helping him with his pranks. Adaptational Nice Guy: Too-Tall's redeeming qualities as aJerk with a Heart of Goldare more prominent in the 2002 series, particularly the later episodes after he's befriended Brother. Bears Are Bad News: As one would expect from the town bully and troublemaker. He also tries to get Brother (and occasionally Fred) to join in on his trouble-making through peer pressure, though they're usually too smart for this. Berserk Button: If you mess with HarryMcGillor get him in trouble, he will make you pay dearly for it. The Big Guy: He is much bigger than his peers — hence the name.

characters.name: Skuzz and Smirk
characters.description: Too-Tall's intimidating right-hand cubs. Flat Character: Their characters in the books aren't really developed much, other than being not as smart as Too-Tall, and being smarter than Vinnie. Only Known by Their Nickname: Everyone calls them Skuzz and Smirk, but their real names are unknown. Only One Name: Their last names have never been given. Number Two: Skuzz is second-in-command of the gang.

characters.name: Vinnie
characters.description: The least intelligent member of Too-Tall's gang with a sharp nose. Aerith and Bob: Of the members of Too-Tall's gang, Vinnie is the only one with a normal name. Demoted to Extra: He makes occasional appearances in the 2002 series and never talks. No Full Name Given: His last name has never been given. Stupid Evil: In the books. Inverted inThe Red Handed Thief, where he’s the only member of the gang who remembers the word "evidence" from Mr. Dweebish's class the previous day.

characters.name: Betsy
characters.description: A skilled athlete from the 2002 TV series, based on Bertha Broom from the Big Chapter Books. No Full Name Given: Her full name has never been given. Tomboy with a Girly Streak: She's a talented athlete who participates in basketball, track... and ballet, while wearing a yellow and pink dress and pink hair ribbons.

characters.name: Ferdinand "Ferdy" Factual
characters.description: Alliterative Name:FerdinandFactual. Generation Xerox: In an interesting take on this trope, he dresses and looks like a smaller version of his uncle, Actual Factual. Homeschooled Kids: His parents are a paleontologist and an archaeologist so he went with them on their digs until he went to live with his uncle Actual Factual. Insufferable Genius: When he first appeared in the series, he would often smugly correct people and look down on his less-intelligent peers. Though he does improve, he never entirely gets rid of it. Meaningful Name: His last name is Factual and he knows a lot of trivia.

characters.name: Milton Chubb
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: Usually, he's a nice, if extremely shy, bear. But if you push hisBerserk Buttonby insulting someone else he likes, he will show off just how powerful he really is. Too-Tall Grizzly and his gang learned this the hard way. Country Mouse: He grew up on a farm, and Beartown is as close to the "big city" as he's ever gotten. Gentle Giant: He's normally a nice, if extremely shy, and extremelylargebear.

characters.name: Bonnie Brown
characters.description: Alliterative Name:BonnieBrown. Just Friends: With Brother Bear, who insists to Sister that she's hisbestfriend, and that that's better than being his girlfriend. They still have plenty ofShip Teasethough.

characters.name: HarryMcGill
characters.description: Don't You Dare Pity Me!: He gets ticked off by anyone who shows sympathy over his being in a wheelchair. It's such a berserk button for him that it leads him to jump to conclusions a few times. Gadgeteer Genius: When first introduced, he's revealed as a computer expert. This later helps him make friends when Brother and Fred figure it out and eventually see justhowgood he is. Handicapped Badass: Has been in a wheelchair since he was involved in a car crash, but is a champion of wheelchair basketball. Odd Friendship: With Too-Tall, after their wheelchair basketball showdown leads to Too-Tall getting respect for him. Smart People Play Chess: He's a very good chess player. This is part of his friendship with Too-Tall Grizzly.

characters.name: Tuffy
characters.description: Abusive Parents: While waiting to see Principal Honeycomb, Tuffy implies that she expects to get spanked if her parents find out that she's been fighting at school. Bad People Abuse Animals:Sistergoes nuts when she catches Tuffy throwing stones at a baby bird trying to fly. Bears Are Bad News: She's a bear cub that is a cruel bully to Sister. The Bully: After tripping Sister, Tuffy beats her up for verbally retaliating. She also makes fun of Brother when he decides not to fight her because she's a girl. Bullying a Dragon: Tuffy makes the dumb choice of giving Sister a mock nickname in front of Brother and then later gives the same nickname in Sister's presence.

characters.name: Teacher Bob
characters.description: The teacher of Brother Bear's 3rd Grade class. Only One Name: His last name is unknown. Reasonable Authority Figure: He's quick to act on poor academic performance or disruptive behavior in his class, but usually is friendly towards his students.

characters.name: Teacher Jane / Scout Leader Jane
characters.description: Deadpan Snarker: In the 1980s series, she has a lot of sarcasm for Papa Bear's foolishness and antics, largely seen in the episodes where she's Bear Scouts leader. I Have Many Names: She's referred to as "Teacher Jane" most of the time, but also as "Scout Leader Jane" in her role as head of the Bear Scouts.The Berenstain Bear Scouts Save That Backscratcheralso refers to her as "Candidate Jane" once after she resigns the Scout Leader position, temporarily, to run for mayor against Horace J. Honeypot.

characters.name: Herbert Honeycomb
characters.description: The principal of Bear Country School. Alliterative Name:HerbertHoneycomb. Reasonable Authority Figure: In contrast to his Vice-Principal'sDean Bittermantendencies, Principal Honeycomb is much more lenient.

characters.name: Mervyn "Bullhorn" Grizzmeyer
characters.description: The stubborn vice principal of Bear Country School. Dean Bitterman: He has very little tolerance for shenanigans and is often the one who doles out discipline, though he can be overruled by Principal Honeycomb. Drunk with Power: When he's made Acting Principal, he immediately establishes a strict dress code, and hisconstantly making it stricternearly drives the students to go on strike. In-Series Nickname: He's known as "Bullhorn" because he doesn't need one to be heard — his booming voice does the trick all on its own. Parental Marriage Veto: He tries this with his son, Mervyn "Mike" Grizzmeyer Junior, in the Big Chapter BookAt Camp Crush, feeling his son and prospective daughter-in-law are too young to be getting married. After they run away to elope though (which they ultimately don't do through with), he eases up and agrees to let them get married when they're ready.

characters.name: Mayor Horace J. Honeypot
characters.description: Permanent Elected Official: He's not always competent and something ofThe Ditherer, but never gets removed from office. The Big Chapter BookGreat Ant Attackimplies this is because he's related to half the bears in Bear Country, so they always vote for him regardless. Spoonerism: In the 1985 series and the Big Chapter Books andBear Scoutschapter books, he tends to get the fronts and backs of his words mixed up. (Example: "What beems to see the bubble — er, seems to be the trouble?") Averted in the main books and the 2002 series, where he speaks normally.

characters.name: Professor Actual Factual
characters.description: Absent-Minded Professor: Occasionally gets so caught up in his work that he forgets to take care of other things. Gentleman and a Scholar: He's been described as one of the kindest, most generous citizens of Bear Country. Mad Libs Dialogue: When he's not rhyming in theLearning At Homeseries, his dialogue usually consists of this. Quite a lot actually to the point of creating a grammar error at least one time: instead of hearing "Find... my birthday," you'll hear "Find...It's my birthday!" Meaningful Name: His last name is Factual and he's a professor. Nephewism: He isn't married, but in the Big Chapter Books, his nephew Ferdy lives with him from time to time when his scientist parents (one an archaeologist, the other a paleontologist) are away on digs.

characters.name: Farmer Ben
characters.description: No Full Name Given: His only known name is "Ben". His wife is even called "Mrs. Ben".The Berenstain Bears and the Haunted Hayrideeventually explains that "Ben" is actually his family name via revealing that his ancestors are Ben Ezra, Ben Abner and Ben Noah, and his son (who's away at college) is Ben Wilmer, but his personal namestillisn't given. Properly Paranoid: Is described as a "suspicious old coot who will count his fingers after shaking hands with you" by Ralph Ripoff. Given Ralph's a local con artist, Ben is quite justified in being suspicious around him.

characters.name: Raffish Ralph / Ralph Ripoff
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: Originally appeared in the TV series and then made a cameo appearance inThe Prize Pumpkin. Later became a recurring antagonist of the Big Chapter Books andBear Scoutschapter books. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He doesn't appear in the 2002 series, due to being in a different continuity. Con Artist: His primary hobby is scamming people. Disney Death: In the Big Chapter BookIn the Freaky Funhouse,two other criminals attempt to murder him when he catches on to their scheme by tying him up and dumping him in a lake. He survives by escaping from the ropes, thanks tohis old days as a magician and escape artist. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: In the Big Chapter BookAnd the Ghost of the Auto Graveyard, the cubs find Ralphtied up and gagged. When they remove the gag, his first word is "Squawk!", much to the cubs' surprise. He has to explain that both he and Squawk, his pet parrot, have been tied up for over a day, and that he's more worried about whether the bird is all right than himself.

characters.name: Bigpaw
characters.description: Bigfoot, Sasquatch, and Yeti: As his name suggests, he is the series'Fictional Counterpartof Bigfoot, though he boasts that he "supersedes" both it and the Yeti during his"I Am" Song. His first appearance even has him leaving behind a paw print, alluding to Bigfoot's trademark footprints. In one episode of the 80's series, he gets mistaken for a Yeti (also known as the "Abominable Snow-Bear" in this universe) when he gets covered in snow while sleepwalking. Characterization Marches On: In his first appearance in "Berenstain Bears Meet Bigpaw", Bigpaw speaks rather normally. In the sequel 80's TV series, he speaks in aThird-Person PersonandYou No Take Candlemanner (though he does speak in first person sometimes). Gaia's Vengeance: He is foretold to be be nature's way of punishing the bears for being too selfish and greedy around Thanksgiving, as he would destroy Bear Country for being too ungrateful for their harvest. In "Meet Bigpaw", thisdoesnearly happen in a roundabout way, since while he never intends to bring harm to the bears at first, when they aggressively march on his home, he nearly kills them all with a rockslide, which would indeed bring forth the destruction of the greedy, paranoid bears as the legend told. It's not until Brother and Sister demonstrate their friendliness and selflessness that Bigpaw and the townspeople both relent, averting the disaster. While Bigpaw didn't destroy the bears as predicted, his coming still taught the townspeople the lesson the legend warned about, fulfilling the prophecy. Gentle Giant: Ultimately proves to be this. When he first meets Brother and Sister, he catches them with his paw as they're falling out of a tree and gently returns them to the ground, and shakes hands with Brother afterward. After this, he only prepares to get violent in self-defense, but stops when he sees the cubs are in danger again. Papa Wolf: Doesnotlike it when the kids are endangered, especially Lizzie and Sister.

characters.name: Two-Ton Grizzly
characters.description: Happily Married: He and his wife Too-Too, who love one another very much and are very much partners in Two-Ton's business. The only time they've ever been shown disagreeing was in the Big Chapter BookAnd the Showdown at Chainsaw Gap, where the pair were on opposite sides during the titular showdown — Two-Ton wanted to keep the new housing development out of "his space", while Too-Too wanted to move into one of the new homes, having gotten tired of the unusual house the family lived in. (Incidentally, Two-Ton would win out in the end, as the family ended up staying in their old home because the new "traditional"-style of house was too different from what they were used to.) Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Two-Ton's plenty gruff and a stern and intimidating authority figure wholooksmean enough (and has proven to have a temper), but he's also an honest and reasonable businessbear who loves his family and is willing to scold his son Too-Tall when Too-Tall's been causing trouble. Meaningful Name: He is very large. Reasonable Authority Figure:In his debut appearance, Two-Ton Grizzly appearsverythreatening at first when he comes stomping out of the woods at Too-Tall, his gang and Brother... and then proceeds to demonstrate that he's a good guy after all when he starts scolding Too-Tall and his gang for trying to make Brother steal from Farmer Ben. This is shown further in the Big Chapter Books, where it's mentioned that he always punishes Too-Tall when he's been caught causing trouble, and in...and the Ghost of the Auto Graveyard, when Brother and Bonnie show up and he mistakenly assumes it's because Too-Tall's been up to no good again....and the Ghost of the Auto Graveyardhas several adult bears state on multiple occasions that despite outward appearances, he's always been an honest businessbear, and they can't imagine himknowinglyreceiving stolen car parts (unwittinglyis another story) or being involved in a ring of car thieves. In his debut appearance, Two-Ton Grizzly appear

characters.name: WeaselMcGreed
characters.description: Big Bad: He's the lead villain of the 1985 cartoon and theScoutschapter books, as he and his followers plot to take over Bear Country. Canon Foreigner: Was first featured in the animated series and was then incorporated into theScoutschapter books. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He and Raffish Ralph are not in the 2002 series, for same reasons as the latter. Hair-Trigger Temper: Can and will start ranting and raving at the slightest provocation and hands out demotions left and right. Informed Species: He and his pack don't really resemble weasels. They look more like grey wolves with cat-like tails instead.

characters.name: Queen Nectar
characters.description: Bee Afraid: Only if you seek her honey. And if you do, she will send out her swarm after you. Reasonable Authority Figure: As much as she dislikes Papa for constantly trying to take her honey, she doesn't believe inSins of the Fatherand is on good terms with the cubs for respecting her. Royals Who Actually Do Something: She is constantly on guard for anyone after the Wild Wild Honey, and she works with other bee colonies when they have their honey stolen. Stock Beehive: Averted. Like real honeybees, her colony nest inside a hollow tree rather than this trope.
